messages.content: I have another museum trip to sort out. The condition review in St. Louis is Tuesday, July 14 at 1:30 p.m., and installation is Wednesday the 15th. I’ll be leaving from Atlanta and traveling alone.
I can compare the practical flight pairings. What time do you need to be at the museum before Tuesday’s review, and how firm is the installation end time on Wednesday?

I should arrive at the museum by 12:45 Tuesday. Wednesday is scheduled to finish at 5:00, but that can slip if the mounts need adjustment. I’m deciding between flying in Monday evening or very early Tuesday, then returning Wednesday night or Thursday morning.

For ATL to STL, the workable nonstops break down this way. On Monday, Delta has a 4:55 p.m. departure arriving at 5:37 p.m. Central, and Southwest has a 7:25 p.m. departure arriving at 8:05 p.m. On Tuesday, Delta has a 6:20 a.m. departure arriving at 7:02 a.m. All three leave enough time for the review, but the Tuesday flight carries more disruption risk because a cancellation or substantial delay could consume most of your margin. From Lambert Airport to the museum area, allow roughly 25 to 35 minutes by car in ordinary traffic.
The Monday Delta flight sounds better than starting at the airport before dawn. What are the return choices?

The latest useful Wednesday nonstop is Southwest at 7:30 p.m., arriving in Atlanta at 10:00 p.m. You would need to leave the museum around 5:35 p.m. to return equipment, reach the airport, and clear security without rushing. That is possible only if installation ends close to schedule. Thursday has a Delta nonstop at 7:00 a.m., arriving at 9:27 a.m., and another at 9:35 a.m., arriving at 12:03 p.m. The 9:35 departure gives you a normal morning and protects against a late Wednesday finish.
Please compare the sensible combinations on price and total trip time. Economy is fine.

The Monday 4:55 p.m. Delta outbound paired with Wednesday’s 7:30 p.m. Southwest return is $358 round trip as separate one-way tickets. It means two hotel nights, but the Wednesday airport transfer is exposed to any installation overrun. Pairing that Delta outbound with Thursday’s 7:00 a.m. Delta return is $386 and requires three hotel nights; you would need to leave a central St. Louis hotel around 5:15 a.m. The same outbound with Thursday’s 9:35 a.m. Delta return is $402, also with three hotel nights, and allows a hotel departure around 7:30 a.m. The Tuesday 6:20 a.m. outbound paired with Wednesday night is lowest at $311 and needs only one hotel night, though it concentrates the operational risk on both ends of the assignment.
Drop the Tuesday outbound. Missing the condition review because of a morning delay is not worth that savings.

That leaves Monday evening arrival as the fixed outbound. Between the returns, Wednesday night saves one hotel night and $44 in airfare, while Thursday at 9:35 a.m. gives the installation meaningful room to run late. The Thursday 7:00 a.m. flight costs $16 less than the 9:35 flight but creates a very early airport transfer after a potentially long installation day.
How tight is Wednesday night if we actually finish at five? I’ll have one checked case with condition-report supplies.

If work ends at 5:00 p.m., packing and signing out could reasonably take 15 to 20 minutes. A car arriving at 5:25 would likely reach the terminal between 5:50 and 6:10. With a checked case, Southwest’s bag cutoff would leave limited tolerance for traffic or a delayed handoff. It works on a clean day, but a slip of even 30 minutes could make the flight impractical.
Then Thursday is the right call. I don’t want everyone watching the clock during installation. Compare the two Thursday flights one more time, including what the hotel dates would be.

Both choices make the hotel stay Monday, July 13 through Thursday, July 16, for three nights. The 7:00 a.m. return gets you home at 9:27 a.m. and costs $386 round trip, but it calls for roughly a 4:45 a.m. wake-up and a 5:15 a.m. hotel departure. The 9:35 a.m. return arrives at 12:03 p.m., costs $402 round trip, and lets you leave the hotel around 7:30. The later flight is the more balanced itinerary after Wednesday’s work.
Use the 9:35 Thursday return as the itinerary for planning. Is it all on Delta, and what would the baggage cost be?

Yes. The pairing is Delta nonstop in both directions: ATL to STL on Monday at 4:55 p.m., arriving 5:37 p.m., and STL to ATL Thursday at 9:35 a.m., arriving 12:03 p.m. The current Main Cabin fare is $402. One standard checked bag would add $35 each way, making the flight total $472 unless your status or payment method waives the fee.
Are seats selectable now?

Yes. Standard seat selection is included with this Main Cabin fare. On the outbound, available choices include 14A and 15A at the window, plus several middle and aisle seats farther back. On the return, 17F and 19A are available at the window. Preferred seats nearer the front cost extra.
Put me in 15A going out and 17F coming back. Window seats are what I want when they’re available. Don’t pay extra to move forward.
I’ve applied 15A outbound and 17F return, both standard window seats with no seat fee. The working itinerary remains $402 before baggage and $472 with one checked case in each direction.
Before we move to hotels, summarize the timing and tell me whether there is any reason to anchor the search differently.

Use Monday, July 13 through Thursday, July 16 for the hotel search. The flight plan is Delta nonstop from Atlanta Monday at 4:55 p.m., landing in St. Louis at 5:37 p.m., followed by Delta nonstop Thursday at 9:35 a.m., landing in Atlanta at 12:03 p.m. Seats 15A and 17F are selected at no charge. The fare is $402, or an estimated $472 with the checked case both ways. This gives you a full night before Tuesday’s 1:30 p.m. condition review and removes Wednesday’s 5:00 p.m. installation finish from the return-flight decision. There is no operational reason to use different hotel dates; a three-night stay near the museum should anchor the next search. The itinerary is selected for planning but has not been ticketed.
